summary: matches=false. Every one of the 11 discrepancies in the previous verdict is resolved, and I confirmed each against the bytes rather than against the fixer's account: the 2017 and 2018 annual bundles were retrieved and re-fetched byte-identical (and all 53 of their members re-hashed), the supersession split was re-derived independently by hashing each per-file capture against its bundle copy, the four substantive revisions (2017 Christmas Bitcoin row and withdrawn grain leg, 2018 July 3 Bitcoin Early Close 12:15, 2018 Dec 25 Bitcoin 'Globex Closed' cell, 2018 Dec 26 Equity 15:15/15:30) were re-read cell by cell, all four revisions of the 2018 New Year's sheet were read row by row, and the two 2016 PDF transcription slips, the mislabelled CDX artifact and the two coverage-prose errors are all corrected. Retrieval integrity is now complete: 167/167 stored hashes reproduce, 8/8 re-fetched documents are byte-identical, 633 xls time tokens and 272 PDF fragments match the cited bytes, ET=CT+1 holds on all 375 rows, no row cites a document from a different year, and fresh unfiltered CDX enumerations of 2017 and 2018 confirm the bundles are the only channel to CME's final revisions. One load-bearing defect remains, and it is a residue of the round-2 re-keying rather than a new error: on 2018-07-03, 2018-11-23 and 2018-12-24 the Grains and Oilseeds verbatim still quotes a sibling row 'MGEX Apple Juice' that CME deleted in the very revisions those rows were re-keyed to, so three claimed quotations cannot be found in their cited documents. No instant, status or family-level value is wrong anywhere in the file. Items 2-4 are minor: one undeclared whitespace/label normalisation, one asymmetrically-omitted Metals TAS note, and a stale title on the shared fix INDEX.
